persona.note: quit my job last week to go all in on our brand. no money yet but honestly ive never felt more alive. i want to stay like this and not lose this fire when it gets hard

understanding.emotion: alive and afraid of losing it
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call starting what is yours to build, and that is where this week begins.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the fire as yours, not borrowed from the quitting.
week_beats.story: A young builder who left everything and faced the first empty month shows you how resolve survives it.

understanding.core_struggle: Has left their job to build a brand with no money yet and wants to keep the fire of feeling alive when it gets hard.
understanding.mirror: You left your job and the money, and for the first time you feel like yourself.
understanding.insight: The fire will not last if you are holding it to feel alive. What will keep it burning is the work itself, not the feeling it gives you.

queries.hook: A fire lit by leaving the safe thing behind; the resolve to build, with no money yet and no looking back.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the feeling of being alive instead of to the work itself; it holds when the work is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do the work fully and well each day, let the feeling go, and keep at it when the fire feels low.
queries.story: A young builder who left everything to build from nothing, faced the first empty month, and kept their resolve through it.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: अलातं तिन्दुकस्येव मुहूर्तमपि हि ज्वल / मा तुषाग्निरिवानर्चिर्धूमायस्व जिजीविषुः
verse.line: Blaze like a torch, even for a moment. Don't just smoulder to stay alive.
verse.translation: Like a torch of tinduka wood, blaze, even if only for a moment. Do not smoulder without flame like a fire of husks, just to stay alive.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: About wholehearted effort, not reckless risk or burnout.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him to blaze like a torch of tinduka wood, even for a moment. She says do not smoulder without flame like a fire of husks, just to stay alive. She wants him to rise and fight, not to linger in despair.
verse.for_you: You felt alive the moment you quit your job. That is your own fire, not just the relief of leaving. Let it burn bright for the work itself, not as proof that you are brave.

verse.speaker: Shandilya
verse.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिꣳल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ॥
verse.line: A person is made of resolve. As you resolve in this life, so you become. So resolve well.
verse.translation: All this is Brahman; from it all arises, into it all dissolves, in it all breathes; so one should meditate on it calmly. A person is made of resolve. As one's resolve is in this world, so one becomes on departing. So let one form a resolve.
verse.meaning: Shandilya is teaching a student about the self. He says that a person is made of resolve. As your resolve is in this world, so you become when you depart. So let a person form a resolve. This means your deepest intention shapes who you are. The life you build is a direct result of the choice you make right now to begin.
verse.for_you: You left your job last week to build this brand. That choice is your resolve. Let it be the thing that forms you, not just the feeling of being alive. The work is the proof of the life you chose.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari tells the reader to remain steady. Let people praise or blame, let money come or go, let death come today or ages hence. The steady do not step off the right path. This means your commitment to your path remains firm regardless of external conditions.
verse.for_you: You have no money yet. That is an external condition. Let their praise or blame, the lack of money, or the fear of losing it not move you a step from the path you chose. Your resolve is the only thing that stays steady.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen, unsure whether to fight. Krishna tells him to act without clinging to what will happen next. He says that on this path, no honest effort is ever wasted. Even a small amount of this practice protects a person from great fear.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week and have never felt more alive. That fire is real, and it will protect you from fear.

verse.speaker: Angada
verse.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
verse.sanskrit: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
verse.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
verse.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verse.why: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

prasang.title: The missed deadline
prasang.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.
prasang.story_hook: They came out of the cave to find that spring had already come, and their deadline had gone.
prasang.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

verse.meaning: Angada speaks to the monkey search party. They are exhausted and have missed their deadline for finding Sita. Angada tells them to keep working, because those who do will see results. He warns that sinking into despair makes it almost impossible to rise again.
verse.for_you: You wonder if your efforts are just stubbornness. Keep working on one small thing today. The results will come, and despair is not the end. Do not let the fear of missing a deadline stop you from starting.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
verse.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
verse.translation: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.meaning: Krisha is telling Arjuna that even those who have found everything still do the work in front of them, not to gain anything, but because the world follows what they do. He says to keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging to the result. That is how you rise. The point is that people copy what you do, not what you say.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week. Now you are building this brand. Keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. Do not chase the feeling of being alive. Let the work itself be the proof.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

story.hook_title: Ram's army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey spoke up

story.for_you: Ram stood on the shore with an army and no way across. Then a quiet monkey said he knew how to build the bridge. Nala admitted his skill, and the whole army hauled trees and rocks for five days. You have the fire, but you do not need to be the only one.

script: You quit your job last week. You have no money yet. You have never felt more alive. But you are already afraid of losing it when the work gets hard.
Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. He has given up. She is angry. Vidula said:
अलातं तिन्दुकस्येव मुहूर्तमपि हि ज्वल / मा तुषाग्निरिवानर्चिर्धूमायस्व जिजीविषुः.
In plain words: Blaze like a torch, even for a moment. Don't just smoulder to stay alive.

This is easier said than done, because the fire you feel is not the work itself. It is the relief of leaving. If you hold it only to feel alive, it will fade. What keeps a torch burning is the wood, not the desire to see light. The work is the wood. The fire is a side effect.
When you sit down to work today, do not ask if you feel alive. Ask if you put in your part. The feeling will follow the work, not the other way around.
What is the one small piece of the work you can claim as yours today?

depth.life: You quit your job last week. You have no money yet. You feel fully alive right now, and you are afraid this feeling will vanish when the work gets hard.
depth.points: The texts say what you are doing is starting what is yours to build. The fire you feel is real, but it is not yours to hold. It is the work itself that will keep you going when the feeling fades.
depth.practice: Notice when you check your phone and feel afraid the fire is dying. Close the screen and do one small task for your brand instead.
depth.question: What is the work itself asking you to do today?
